newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway all-share index drops, but Fokus Bank rises.
newsitem.headline: Norway all-share index drops, but Fokus Bank rises.

text.p: Takeover target Fokus Bank was the most traded share on the Norwegian stock exchange on Monday with dealers suggesting a competitor was buying the share.
Oslo's Total index closed 0.23 percent lower at 1,082.01 points in turnover of 1.01 billion crowns, including 421 million in Fokus, or 8.8 percent of its stock.
The share rose 3.55 percent to 73 crowns, the price at which savings-bank group Sparebankgruppen has offered to buy Norway's fourth largest bank.
The share has been hovering just above or below the 73-crown mark since the hostile takeover bid was made on April 14.

Dealers said word was that savings bank Union Bank of Norway was buying Fokus stock but the strategy behind such a purchase was unclear and the bank refused comment on the speculations. Fokus is 80 percent owned by foreign investors.

DnB was up 0.79 percent at 25.50 crowns, Christiania Bank fell 1.7 percent to 23.50 and insurer Storebrand slipped two percent to 43.50 crowns the day before their first-quarter announcements on Tuesday morning.
